content:
Foxtale could have signed anyone.

a fitness icon. a young female actress, like every known beauty brand. someone whose entire identity is looking good and being seen looking good.

they signed Shah Rukh Khan. a 60 year old man who has never once made looking good seem like the point.

and that is exactly why it works.

here's the honest marketing truth first. you don't sign Shah Rukh Khan to sell a product. you sign him because you want the entire country to stop and notice you exist. i mentioned foxtale to a few people around me today who had never heard of the brand. the moment i showed them the campaign they recognised it immediately. not because of foxtale. because of who was in it. that kind of awareness would take a young D2C brand years to build. SRK compressed it into one launch.

but the more interesting move is cultural.

men's skincare in india has always asked men to either not care or pretend they don't. the ads made it clinical so it felt like solving a problem, or rugged so nobody had to admit they actually cared. either way, caring about your skin needed a costume to be acceptable.

SRK doesn't wear the costume; he never has. he is comfortable, specific, entirely himself in a way that doesn't ask for your validation or offer an explanation. putting him at the centre of a skincare campaign doesn't feel like a men's grooming ad. it feels like a person who simply likes himself.

and that, in 2026, is the most radical thing a skincare brand could put on a billboard.

foxtale's campaign says let your glow through. they needed someone whose glow you already believed in before the product entered the conversation.

in hindsight, it couldn't have been anyone else.
